paper_metadata.title: A Quantum Online Portfolio Optimization Algorithm

experiments.description: Theoretical sampling-based online portfolio optimization algorithm that replaces full investment in all assets with ℓ1-sampling from the current portfolio vector, while still using the exact exponentiated-gradient update on the full price-relative vector.

hyperparameters.s: number of samples per time step
hyperparameters.rmin: known lower bound on price relatives

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical ℓ1-sampling data structure is built for the current portfolio vector w^(t); the algorithm samples s asset indices from w^(t) and invests equally across sampled assets.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Online portfolio selection maximizing average log wealth LS = (1/T) sum_t log(w^(t) · rho^(t)) under exponentiated-gradient updates.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No short-selling; portfolio vectors remain on the simplex. Sampling affects only executed trades, not the full update.

problem_instance.description: Abstract online portfolio-selection setting with adversarially revealed price-relative vectors over T rounds.

dataset_specification.description: No concrete market dataset is used; the paper analyzes an abstract online setting with price relatives rho^(t) satisfying rmin <= rho_i^(t) <= 1.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct ℓ1-sampling data structure for w^(t); sample s indices i_1^(t), ..., i_s^(t) from w^(t).
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute the sampled wealth factor (1/s) sum_l rho_{i_l^(t)}^(t) and update the full portfolio vector using EG(eta).

speedup_claims.conditions: sampling-based execution with s samples per time step
speedup_claims.caveats: Runtime worsens to O(T^2 n log(T/delta)); only transaction cost improves.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(T^2 n log(T/delta)) time and O(T^2 C log(T/delta)) transaction cost for the sampling-based classical algorithm.

experiments.description: Approximate sampling-based online portfolio optimization that estimates the inner product w^(t) · rho^(t) classically with multiplicative error before performing the exponentiated-gradient update.

hyperparameters.s: number of samples per time step
hyperparameters.rmin: known lower bound on price relatives
hyperparameters.epsilon_I: relative error for inner-product estimation, set to 3 eta / (4 rmin)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Uses classical ℓ1-sampling for trade execution and classical sampling-based inner-product estimation for the update.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Online portfolio selection with erroneous exponentiated-gradient update using approximate inner product and exact normalization.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No short-selling; simplex constraint maintained by exponentiated-gradient update.

problem_instance.description: Abstract online portfolio-selection setting with sequentially revealed price-relative vectors.

dataset_specification.description: No concrete dataset; analysis assumes price relatives bounded by rmin and 1.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: ℓ1-sample from w^(t); estimate w^(t) · rho^(t) via repeated classical sampling (median-of-means).
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Use the estimated inner product in the erroneous exponentiated-gradient update; compute sampled wealth factor and regret bound.

speedup_claims.conditions: classical inner-product estimation via repeated sampling
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an approximate classical variant; it is introduced mainly as a bridge to the quantum algorithm.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(Tn + T^2/(rmin) log(1/delta) + T^2 log(T/delta)) time, as stated in the paper for Algorithm 3.

experiments.description: Quantum online portfolio optimization algorithm using quantum state preparation, quantum norm estimation, quantum inner-product estimation, and quantum multi-sampling to implement an online exponentiated-gradient portfolio update.

hyperparameters.s: number of samples per time step
hyperparameters.eta: learning rate, set to 2 rmin sqrt(2 log n / T)
hyperparameters.rmin: known lower bound on price relatives
hyperparameters.epsilon_I: relative error for quantum inner-product estimation, set to 3 eta / (4 rmin)
hyperparameters.epsilon_Z: relative error for quantum norm estimation, set to eta^2 / rmin^2

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initialize U_rho^(0) = I, I_tilde = 1, q^(1) = (1, ..., 1), and U_q^(1) = I.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Price relatives are provided via quantum oracles U_rho^(t) acting as |j>|0> -> |j>|rho_j^(t)>; portfolio vectors are represented implicitly through q^(t) and normalized via quantum state preparation.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Online portfolio selection maximizing average log wealth under exponentiated-gradient updates with approximate inner products and normalization.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No short-selling; simplex constraint enforced through normalized exponentiated-gradient updates.
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: O(T) ancilla qubits for gains and ratios in Lemma 2; exact count not specified.

problem_instance.description: Abstract online portfolio-selection problem with sequentially revealed price-relative oracles.

dataset_specification.description: No concrete market dataset; the paper assumes online access to price-relative oracles at each time step.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: O(log n) for the asset index register plus O(T) ancilla qubits in Lemma 2; exact total not specified.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare q^(t), estimate q_max, estimate ||q^(t)/q_max||_1, prepare approximate portfolio state, determine heavy coordinates, and perform quantum multi-sampling.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Query the price-relative oracle for sampled indices, estimate inner products, and update q^(t+1) via arithmetic circuits.

speedup_claims.conditions: using quantum state preparation, quantum norm estimation, quantum inner-product estimation, and quantum multi-sampling
speedup_claims.caveats: The stated runtime is asymptotic and includes polylog factors hidden in O~; practical QRAM/oracle construction may dominate.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: The paper states total runtime O~(T^3 sqrt(n/rmin) log^{1.5}(1/delta)) and quadratic speedup in n relative to the classical approximate algorithm.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(Tn + T^2/(rmin) log(1/delta) + T^2 log(T/delta)) time for the approximate classical algorithm; the earlier sampling-based classical algorithm is O(T^2 n log(T/delta)).
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: 12/rmin in the regret bound relative to the optimal offline gain.
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_classical: 8/rmin in the regret bound for the approximate classical algorithm; 2/rmin for the sampling-based classical algorithm.
